html:
Aristophanes was the great comic playwright of Athens, born about 446 BCE. He wrote about forty plays, and eleven survive. They are the best examples we have of Old Comedy, a wild, rude and openly political form of theatre.

He wrote mostly during the Peloponnesian War, and the war runs through his work. His plays mocked generals and politicians by name, above all the popular leader Cleon, who took him to court over one of them. Among the survivors:

  • The Knights (424 BCE), an attack on Cleon
  • The Clouds (423 BCE), which mocked Socrates
  • The Birds (414 BCE), about a city built in the sky
  • Lysistrata (411 BCE), a comedy about ending the war
  • The Frogs (405 BCE), a contest in the underworld between Aeschylus and Euripides

His later plays, written after Athens lost the war, are milder. Plato made him a guest in the Symposium, telling the myth that lovers are two halves of one being. He died about 386 BCE.
sum: Aristophanes was the great comic playwright of Athens, born about 446 BCE. He wrote about forty plays, and eleven survive. They are the best examples we have of Old Comedy, a wild, rude and openly political form of theatre.
